Definition: properly, to sever oneself, i.e. (by implication) to be dislocated; figuratively, to abandon; causatively, to impale (and thus allow to drop to pieces by rotting)
BiblicalUsage: Yâqa means to be torn apart, to be dislocated, and by extension to abandon or to hang up. The Gibeonites demanded seven sons of Saul to hang before the LORD, and the prophet says Jerusalem's mind was alienated from her lovers after they defiled her.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that what is torn from God will not hold, and the same word that speaks of a dislocated joint speaks of a faithless heart.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
